subroutines.name: plot_sprite
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite
subroutines.description: Copy sprite sprite_number to the screen with its top-left corner at byte column plot_x, pixel row plot_y. The sprite tables give the address of its data and its size; the data is stored row by row, sprite_width bytes to a row, and is written over the screen contents without masking. The screen is laid out like MODE 2 with 640-byte character rows from &3000, so successive bytes of a sprite row are 8 bytes apart, and each pixel row starts one byte below the last, or 640-7 bytes on when it crosses into the next character row.

subroutines.name: screen_address
subroutines.title: Calculate the screen address of plot_x, plot_y
subroutines.description: The game's screen_address, reading the screen's row offsets from Table (row_offsets, &C675), which BOOT's *DUNJUNZ or this editor's *L. TABLE puts in private RAM.

subroutines.name: editor_start
subroutines.title: *EDITOR: copy the plotter page and start
subroutines.description: Copy &2700-&28FF to &0900-&0AFF (the plotter, screen_address, the item types and checksums, and the sprite tables), freeing &2700 for the level file, then start.

subroutines.name: editor_init
subroutines.title: Set up and choose a level
subroutines.description: Disable ESCAPE, point the BREAK intercept at break_to_start and BRKV at MOS 3.20's reset entry (so any error restarts the machine), load Table the first time, set the cursor keys and *TV255 1, select MODE 7 and ask whether to edit a level or start a new one. To edit, choose disc or tape and the file, and *LOAD it at &2700.

subroutines.name: ask_key
subroutines.title: Print a prompt and wait for one of its keys
subroutines.description: Print the text at XY up to its '*', flush the input buffer and scan the keyboard until an answer is pressed. With A=0 the answers are the two keys whose internal numbers are in scratch and scratch_hi, and A returns 0 or 1. Otherwise the answers are the digits 0-3 (drive_keys), and the digit is printed.

on_entry.A: 0 for two keys, else a drive digit

on_exit.A: 0 or 1 for the key pressed (A=0 on entry)

subroutines.name: new_lines
subroutines.title: Print a new line and a blank line
subroutines.description: CR, LF, LF.

subroutines.name: ask_filename
subroutines.title: Ask for a filename
subroutines.description: Pause, flush the input buffer, prompt and read up to seven characters into filename_buffer. If nothing is typed, the name is L.

on_exit.scratch: the name's length, with its CR

subroutines.name: new_level
subroutines.title: Start a new, empty level
subroutines.description: Fill the level's wall block with &03, then set up the editing screen as for a loaded level.

subroutines.name: start_editing
subroutines.title: Set up the editing screen and edit
subroutines.description: Clear the wall map and the item slots, select MODE 2 with no cursor and 30 rows, copy unpack_level and free_cell to &7B00 and &7D80, mark every cell object-free and every link unused, and zero the counts. For a loaded level, decrypt it, drop any object of type &73 (the Chalice, which only level 25 has and the editor has no sprite for), unpack it and draw it. Then clear the level file's tables, ready for saving, and run the editing loop.

subroutines.name: edit_loop
subroutines.title: The editing loop
subroutines.description: Each pass: wait three frames when the slow cursor is on; f0 toggles it. SHIFT+S saves, once the exit, all eight trapdoors and a key for every door are placed. Then move the cursor (',' '.' 'A' 'Z'), flash it when placing walls, change colour 10 (cursor up and down), choose the item ('1' and '2'), place it (SPACE, repeating while held), delete what is under the cursor (TAB) and show the door-key links while CTRL is held.

subroutines.name: check_door_keys
subroutines.title: Check that every door has its key
subroutines.description: Count the links in use and compare with door_count.

on_exit.Z: set if every door has a key

subroutines.name: key_pressed
subroutines.title: Test a key
subroutines.description: OSBYTE &81 with the INKEY number in X.

on_exit.Z: set if the key is pressed

subroutines.name: choose_filing_system
subroutines.title: Ask for disc or tape
subroutines.description: Disc: *DISC, then ask for the drive (0-3) and *DRIVE it. Tape: *TAPE.

subroutines.name: set_edit_screen
subroutines.title: Send edit_screen_vdu
subroutines.description: No cursor, 30 rows, and colours 10 and 9.

subroutines.name: crypt_level
subroutines.title: Encrypt or decrypt the level file
subroutines.description: Exclusive-OR each byte of &2700-&29AF with the low byte of its address, as the game's decrypt_level does at &6B00. Doing it twice restores the bytes.

subroutines.name: set_colour_10
subroutines.title: Show logical colour 10 as the chosen colour
subroutines.description: VDU 19,10,n,0,0,0 with n from colour_10.

subroutines.name: show_labels
subroutines.title: Print the counts' labels
subroutines.description: In colour 1, at column 16: Objs, Mons and Dors.

subroutines.name: show_counts
subroutines.title: Print the counts
subroutines.description: Objects at (17, 2), trapdoors at (17, 6) and doors at (17, 10).

subroutines.name: show_cursor_position
subroutines.title: Print the cursor's cell

subroutines.name: print_number
subroutines.title: Print a two-digit number at a text position
subroutines.description: Move the text cursor to (X, Y) with VDU 31 and print A (0-99) as two digits.

subroutines.name: wall_edges
subroutines.title: Put walls round the edge of the map
subroutines.description: Place a wall in every cell of columns 0 and 31 and rows 0 and 47, as every level has.

subroutines.name: save_level
subroutines.title: Save the level
subroutines.description: Point the BREAK intercept at break_to_save, ask for the level's number (nothing typed: catalogue the disc), take its checksum from level_checksums, set the level's first byte so that its bytes sum to that, encrypt it, choose disc or tape and the filename, *SAVE it and offer another level. Levels 1-24 can be saved; level 25 is in Stones.

subroutines.name: catalogue
subroutines.title: Catalogue the disc or tape
subroutines.description: Show CAT after the prompt, choose disc or tape, *CAT, show the disc's free space with Table's routine, then ask for the level number again.

subroutines.name: choose_wall_block
subroutines.title: Choose the level's wall block
subroutines.description: Clear the screen, show 25 rows, load Stones (the 24 wall blocks) at &6E80, draw them in a grid of four by six and frame the chosen one. Move the frame with ',' '.' (one) and 'A' 'Z' (a row); SPACE copies the chosen block into the level's wall block.

subroutines.name: draw_wall_blocks
subroutines.title: Draw the 24 wall blocks
subroutines.description: Plot sprites &12-&29 at their places in the grid.

subroutines.name: move_chooser
subroutines.title: Move the chosen wall block
subroutines.description: '.' and ',' move one block on or back, 'Z' and 'A' a row of four; a move off the grid is undone.

subroutines.name: chooser_key_pressed
subroutines.title: Test a key
subroutines.description: OSBYTE &81 with the INKEY number in X, as key_pressed.

subroutines.name: block_place
subroutines.title: Find a wall block's place in the grid
subroutines.description: Block n is at column n mod 4, row n div 4: plot_x = 8 x column + &1A, plot_y = 24 x row + &14.

subroutines.name: frame_block
subroutines.title: Draw or erase the frame round the chosen block
subroutines.description: Plot sprite A (&2A the frame, &2B a blank) one byte left of and two rows above the chosen block, then plot the block again.

subroutines.name: show_25_rows
subroutines.title: Show 25 rows

subroutines.name: pack_items
subroutines.title: Pack the item slots into the level file
subroutines.description: Go through the slots from the last (&4F) to the first, so that the tables come out in the reverse of the order unpack_level read them: objects into entries 1 upwards (the exit always into entry 30), trapdoors into entries 0-7, and each door with its linked key into the next door entry. Keys and free slots are skipped.

subroutines.name: pack_level
subroutines.title: Pack the level for saving
subroutines.description: Pack the item slots, then copy the wall map and the object-free map into the level file.

subroutines.name: load_stones
subroutines.title: Load the wall blocks
subroutines.description: *LOAD STONES (at its own address, &6E80) with VDU output off.

subroutines.name: move_cursor
subroutines.title: Move the cursor
subroutines.description: Wait for the frame, rub out the cursor and put back what is under it, move with ',' '.' 'A' 'Z' within the 32 by 48 map, and plot the current item there as the cursor.

subroutines.name: plot_at_cursor
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: At screen byte column 2x and pixel row 5y.

subroutines.name: item_at_cursor
subroutines.title: Find what is in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: Search the slots for an item at the cursor; failing that, look at the wall map.

on_exit.A: the item's sprite and X its slot; 0 for a wall; &FF for nothing

subroutines.name: wall_bit
subroutines.title: Find the cursor's bit in the wall map
subroutines.description: As the game lays out its maps: the byte at (y AND &F8) x 4 + (y AND 7) + (x AND &F8), bit 7 - (x AND 7).

subroutines.name: put_item
subroutines.title: Put the current item in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: Clear the cell's object-free bit. A wall sets the wall map's bit; anything else takes a free slot, and a key is recorded as the key of the link being made.

subroutines.name: remove_at_cursor
subroutines.title: Remove what is in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: Free an item's slot, or clear a wall's bit in the wall map.

subroutines.name: place_item
subroutines.title: Place the current item at the cursor
subroutines.description: In an empty cell, place the current item within the limits: one exit, eight trapdoors, 20 doors (a door is also a wall), 29 objects, and a key only when a door is waiting for one, which links the two. With a key chosen, SPACE on an unlinked door makes it the door waiting for its key.

subroutines.name: restore_waiting_door
subroutines.title: Show the waiting door as it was
subroutines.description: Put the waiting door's own sprite back in its slot and plot it.

subroutines.name: plot_slot
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite at a slot's cell
subroutines.description: At screen byte column 2x and pixel row 5y of slot X's cell.

subroutines.name: find_free_link
subroutines.title: Find a free door-key link
subroutines.description: The highest link whose door is &FF.

subroutines.name: free_slot
subroutines.title: Free a slot
subroutines.description: Zero its item and position.

subroutines.name: delete_item
subroutines.title: Delete what is in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: Uncount the item and remove it. Deleting a door removes its key too, and deleting a key removes its door (and the door's wall). A waiting door is left alone. A wall is cleared.

subroutines.name: line_x_to_graphics
subroutines.title: Convert line_x to graphics x
subroutines.description: line_gx = line_x x 32: a cell is two screen bytes, four MODE 2 pixels, 32 graphics units wide. (delete_item also falls into it, harmlessly, when a key has no link.)

subroutines.name: line_y_to_graphics
subroutines.title: Convert line_y to graphics y
subroutines.description: line_gy = &3FF - line_y x 20: a cell is five pixel rows, 20 graphics units, counted down from the top of the screen.

subroutines.name: plot_line_point
subroutines.title: PLOT to a cell
subroutines.description: VDU 25 with plot code X and the graphics position of (line_x, line_y).

subroutines.name: draw_links
subroutines.title: Draw each door-key link as a line
subroutines.description: For each link in use, PLOT 68 at the door's cell and PLOT 5 to its key's: exclusive-OR lines (GCOL 3), so drawing them again rubs them out.

subroutines.name: cursor_key_pressed
subroutines.title: Test a key
subroutines.description: OSBYTE &81 with the INKEY number in X, as key_pressed.

subroutines.name: unpack_level
subroutines.title: Unpack the loaded level into the slots
subroutines.description: Read the level file's tables from the last entry back, putting each item in the next slot down from &4F: objects (with their editor items found from item_types), each door and then its key (linked), and the trapdoors. Copy the wall map and object-free map. Count the objects and doors.

subroutines.name: item_for_type
subroutines.title: Find the editor's item for a level type
subroutines.description: Search item_types from entry 1 for the type. A type with no item would search on into the bytes beyond.

subroutines.name: free_cell
subroutines.title: Mark the cursor's cell as holding an object
subroutines.description: Clear its bit in the object-free map (laid out as the wall map).

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes after unpack_level's image.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes, among them the text PAGE.

banners.name: break_to_start
banners.title: BREAK intercept: start again
banners.description: Called twice during a reset; on the second call, with C set, go back to editor_init, keeping the editor in memory.

banners.name: edit_or_new_prompt
banners.title: Prompts and commands
banners.description: Prompts end with '*' (for ask_key) or a zero (printed by callers); commands end with CR. load_command's filename is copied in from the filename buffer.

banners.name: break_to_save
banners.title: BREAK intercept: back to saving
banners.description: Called twice during a reset; on the second call, with C set, go back to save_level, keeping the packed level in memory.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes: a fragment of BBC BASIC assembler.

banners.title: The chooser's frame
banners.description: Sprite &2A: 6 bytes by 18 pixel rows.

banners.name: sprite_addr_lo
banners.title: Sprite tables
banners.description: Each of the editor's 51 sprites' data address (low and high bytes), width in bytes and height in pixel rows. 0-&0F are the items (two bytes by five rows, at &2A00), &10 is blank (zeros at &7FF0), &11 a door waiting for its key, &12-&29 the 24 wall blocks in Stones (&6E80), &2A the wall-block chooser's frame and &2B a blank part of the screen that erases it, and &2C the cursor. Entries &2D-&32 are not used.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes, covered by the level file (&2700-&29AF) when one is loaded.

banners.title: Sprites
banners.description: The cursor (sprite &2C), then the 16 items (sprites 0-&0F) and the door waiting for its key (&11), each two bytes by five pixel rows.

banners.title: Clear the cursor's wall
banners.description: Clear its bit in the wall map.

memory_map.description: Address of a map byte, high byte.

memory_map.description: INKEY number of the cursor-up key: 'A' (&BE).

memory_map.name: key_down
memory_map.description: INKEY number of the cursor-down key: 'Z' (&9E).

memory_map.name: object_count
memory_map.description: Objects placed (at most 29).

memory_map.description: Each item slot's y.

memory_map.description: Each item slot's editor sprite (0: free).

memory_map.name: line_y
memory_map.description: The cell a link line is drawn from or to, y.

memory_map.name: line_gx
memory_map.description: That cell's graphics x, low byte (high byte at &0DD3).

memory_map.name: line_gx_hi
memory_map.description: That cell's graphics x, high byte.

memory_map.name: line_gy
memory_map.description: That cell's graphics y, low byte (high byte at &0DD5).

memory_map.name: line_gy_hi
memory_map.description: That cell's graphics y, high byte.

memory_map.name: pending_door_item
memory_map.description: The sprite of the door waiting for its key, or &FF if none.

memory_map.name: pending_door_slot
memory_map.description: The slot of the door waiting for its key.

memory_map.name: link_index
memory_map.description: The door-key link being made: an index into link_door and link_key.

memory_map.name: link_door
memory_map.description: Each of 20 door-key links' door slot, or &FF if unused.

memory_map.name: link_key
memory_map.description: Each door-key link's key slot.

memory_map.name: wall_map
memory_map.description: The wall map being edited (the level's &C9 bytes, laid out as in the game).

memory_map.name: unpack_slot
memory_map.description: unpack_level's next free slot, counting down.

memory_map.name: unpack_link
memory_map.description: unpack_level's next free link, counting down.

memory_map.name: wall_blocks
memory_map.description: Stones, loaded here by choose_wall_block: the 24 wall blocks (&30 bytes each) that a level can use.

memory_map.name: object_free_map
memory_map.description: The object-free map being edited (&C9 bytes): a clear bit marks a cell where an object may lie.

memory_map.name: blank_sprite
memory_map.description: Zeros, plotted as the blank sprite &10.

memory_map.name: row_offsets
memory_map.description: In Table: the screen's character row offsets, high byte then low byte (a copy of MOS 1.20's table at &C375).

memory_map.name: show_free_space
memory_map.description: In Table: the routine that *CAT is followed by, which prints the disc's free space (*FREE).

memory_map.name: mos320_reset_entry
memory_map.description: MOS 3.20's reset entry, the target of the 6502 reset vector.
